Issued at 1235 AM CDT Thu Oct 15 2026

Today: Rain Across Much of the Area

Our next pair of synoptic features that will be responsible for
widespread rainfall today can be noted on GOES-19 water vapor 
imagery and RAP 500mb heights as both an upper-level low situated
over Colorado begins to phase with a northern stream upper- 
level trough moving into the northern Great Plains. As this 
occurs, much of deterministic guidance generally agrees on 
instigating surface cyclogenesis south of the local area at the
exit region of this upper-level feature as it pivots through 
the region. Additionally, a fairly respectable plume of low- 
level moisture pushes just south of the local area with some 
increase in precipitable waters to around 1-1.5" this afternoon.
Consequently, the recent HREF generally has respectable 
rainfall amounts with the inter-quartile range for QPF amounts 
across the region ranging from 0.5" to 1". As far as timing is 
concerned, much of the CAMs generally agree on bringing 
precipitation associated with this system into the region 
towards daybreak. As we head through the day, cannot rule out 
some weak convection south of I-90 where some weak MUCAPE is 
present in the RAP which may lead to some locally heavier 
rainfall amounts (higher percentiles of the HREF have some 
1.5-2" amounts in Clayton and Grant Counties). Otherwise, the 
main cold front with this system swings through the region by 
mid-evening ending precipitation potential from west to east. 
Overall, should be a healthy rainfall event but not expecting 
much impacts from this rainfall. 

Friday: Breezy Conditions with Morning Showers Possible

Behind the aforementioned cold front on Friday, the combination of 
an increasing surface pressure gradient and some mixing into a 40 kt 
low-level jet will allow for winds to increase to around 15-25 mph 
with gusts upwards of 35-45 mph, particularly west of the 
Mississippi River. While probabilities in the NBM are not 
overly high (10-30%) for wind gusts over 45 mph, some 
instability and steep low-level lapse rates are present in RAP 
soundings. As a result, this should allow for some showers to 
push through the region on Friday morning associated with the 
cyclonic flow of the upper-level trough overhead. Consequently, 
would not be surprised to see some local enhancement of winds as
showers aid in momentum transferring down some stronger gusts 
to the surface where gusts reaching 45 mph would be possible. 

Friday Night - Saturday Morning: Frost/Freeze Likely

By the time the nighttime hours roll around on Friday, the 
aforementioned surface pressure gradient begins to wane as surface 
high pressure begins to push into the local area. Consequently, 
expecting winds to decrease with clearing skies as well. Therefore, 
the setup looks fairly solid for an effective radiational cooling 
night across the region with the NBM having fairly high 
probabilities (60-100%) for lows to fall below freezing across the 
entire local area outside of river valley locations. As a result, 
Frost Advisories and Freeze Warnings will likely be needed during 
this period. The highest probabilities (60-90%) in the NBM for a 
killing freeze with lows below 28 degrees will generally be near and 
north of I-94, with lower probabilities elsewhere (10-40%). 

This Weekend & Early Next Week: Dry, Gradually Warming Up 

As we head into the weekend and early next week, upper-level ridging 
will push into the region allowing for increasing southerly to 
southwesterly flow in the low-levels. As a result, expecting the 
advection of a modestly warmer airmass into the region during this 
period. Consequently, temperatures warm into the 60s by Sunday with 
highs even jumping back into the lower 70s as suggested in the 
median high temperatures fields of the NBM by early next week. 
Overall with the upper-level ridging overhead, not seeing much
for precipitation chances in ensemble guidance as the grand 
ensemble (GEFS/EC/Canadian ensemble) has very low (under 10% 
chance) measurable precipitation probabilities this weekend 
through Tuesday of next week.
